{{Quote|Qwi, you were always so brilliant&mdash;but in other ways you managed to be incredibly dense.|Bevel Lemelisk|<ref name="Dk61">[[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']], Chapter 61</ref>}}
The '''Omwati''' were lithe [[near-Human]]s with [[Color/Legends|blue]] skin and a [[Bird/Legends|bird]]-like appearance. They were native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Omwat/Legends|Omwat]] and were known for their intellect and natural talent for science, [[Engineer/Legends|engineering]], and [[Music/Legends|music]]. Omwati children had incredibly pliant minds that, with the proper training, could retain data and be educated beyond the threshold of most other [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]].

A number of Omwati joined the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], but contact between their planet and the [[galactic community]] was lost at a later point. It was eventually restored when the planet was rediscovered by [[Republic officer/Legends|Republic officer]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]], who, while later serving the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], [[Death/Legends|killed]] thousands of Omwati in a scheme to transform the survivors into great developers of weapons technology. After Tarkin's [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|death]] and the fall of the Empire, the Omwati developed their own [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] and, with some initial misunderstanding due to their natural naivete, joined the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. Some Omwati were particularly motivated by Tarkin's destructive actions on their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].

Throughout their history, several Omwati exhibited [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitivity]], and different Omwati took up various traditions of using [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], including becoming [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] and [[Shaman/Legends|shamans]]. After joining the New Republic, they even developed [[Omwati Force tradition|their own Force tradition]], which was taught on Omwat.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|I will not be number two to some feather-brained&mdash;|[[Iella Wessiri Antilles|Iella Wessiri]], about Qwi Xux|<ref name="XW">''[[X-Wing: Starfighters of Adumar]]'', Chapter 1</ref>}}
The Omwati were a [[near-Human]] [[Species/Legends|species]]<ref name="TS6" /> of lithe, fragile [[Humanoid/Legends|anthropoids]].<ref name="AAUAA" /> In both [[Gender/Legends|sexes]], the Omwati's lack of sturdiness was readily apparent,<ref name="UAA" /> and females were even more willowy than males.<ref name="AAUAA" /> Adult Omwati grew to a height between 1.6 and 2.1 [[Meter/Legends|meters]],<ref name="AAUAA" /> with females feasibly falling below this range to be as short as 1.49 meters.<ref name="L1">''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]''</ref> Omwati skin was [[Color/Legends|blue]],<ref name="AAUAA" /> commonly a lighter shade<ref name="T1" /><ref name="L1" /><ref name="GC">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'' {{C|Under ''Qwi Xux''}}</ref> that darkened during occasional outbursts of emotion, such as blushing or feeling anger.<ref name="Dk61" />

[[File:Qwi_Xux_Headshot.jpg|thumb|left|150px|An Omwati]]
The heads of the Omwati were covered by feathery threads similar to down, a matter that also composed the species' eyebrows. This sparkling,<ref name="T1" /> gossamer-like substance could be any color from [[Color/Legends|red]]-blond to pearl [[Color/Legends|white]],<ref name="AAUAA" /> and was commonly iridescent.<ref name="L1" /> Some individuals [[Hair dye|dyed]] these threads to reach shades beyond that spectrum,<ref name="L7">''[[Legacy of the Force: Fury]]'', Chapter 2</ref> partly because it could be pale enough to appear almost transparent.<ref name="L1" />

Omwati tended to have delicate facial features<ref name="L1" /> that were accented gracefully by their blue skin.<ref name="XW" /> The face of an Omwati was usually small, elfin,<ref name="T1" /><ref name="Dk30">[[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']], Chapter 30</ref> and [[Bird/Legends|bird]]-like,<ref name="T1" /> which gave them an exotic attractiveness without sacrificing their [[Human/Legends|Human]]-like aspect.<ref name="Dk30" /> Mature individuals could maintain a youthful appearance, their age betrayed only by their [[Eye/Legends|eyes]].<ref name="CJ18">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']], Chapter 18</ref> Omwati had proportionally large eyes<ref name="L1" /> that gave them excellent vision.<ref name="Dk30" /> Their most common eye colors were blue&mdash;which could be of many distinct shades<ref name="AAUAA" />&mdash;and indigo.<ref name="T1" /> Omwati were also characterized by their high, [[Flute/Legends|flute]]-like voices<ref name="T1" /><ref name="CJ18" /> that sometimes sounded [[Music/Legends|musical]], like birdsong.<ref name="T1" />

The Omwati [[Brain/Legends|brain]] was highly developed. Omwati were able to achieve great intellectual feats in the sciences and arts.<ref name="Reb">[[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|''Star Wars: Rebellion'']] {{C|Under ''Omwat''}}</ref> However, young Omwati had to be coached and encouraged to become creatively brilliant, or they would never reach their potential. In addition, too much pressure could easily collapse a promising young Omwati's mind.<ref name="T1" /> The species began their adolescence at thirteen [[Galactic Standard Calendar|years]] of age, were biologically mature at eighteen, and started feeling the ill effects of old age at forty-one, which only increased at sixty-six. They had a lifespan of eighty-five years.<ref name="AAUAA" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Don't know her well enough to form an opinion, but her playthings have made quite an impression.|Corran Horn, on Qwi Xux|<ref name="I, Jedi">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Tannis.jpg|thumb|right|110px|A female Omwati]]
Naturally [[Sentience/Legends|intelligent]] and perceptive, the Omwati had great skill at solving abstract problems, and they felt proud of their customary review of past lessons while planning for the future.<ref name="UAA" /> Children were particularly adept at memorizing and processing information; young Omwati commonly had a great potential as [[Engineer/Legends|engineers]] if provided with the correct training.<ref name="TS6" /> Those Omwati who did not feel like following this path still had advanced skills in [[Computer/Legends|computer]] operation and advanced machine [[Technician/Legends|maintenance and repair]]. The graceful Omwati placed great stock in the concept of friendship, second only to their concept of the family.<ref name="AAUAA" /> Their [[Homeworld/Legends|home planet]], [[Omwat/Legends|Omwat]],<ref name="AAUAA" /> was covered by [[honeycomb settlement]]s, the [[City/Legends|city]]-like constructions that the species utilized.<ref name="T1" />

Omwati had an elegant language, [[Omwatese]], which had unusual tonal inflections. It was written using a fluid script of jigsaw-like letters.<ref name="UAA" /> Most Omwati learned to speak and read [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] as a second language.<ref name="AAUAA" /> Keyboards with letters were not to their liking, as members of the species preferred music to words as a computer data input method.<ref name="TS6" /> Certain Omwati had two-part names, such as Helix Lur, Xel Tanni, and [[Qwi Xux]]. Others went by only one name, such as Girral, Orthan, and Zallir.<ref name="UAA" />

==History==
{{Quote|My home planet was Omwat, in the Outer Rim. Moff Tarkin took ten young Omwati children from various cities. He placed us in intense forced-education camps, trying to mold us into great designers and problem solvers.|Qwi Xux|<ref name="T1" />}}
[[File:Qwi.jpg|thumb|left|120px|Qwi Xux, a female Omwati]]
The Omwati evolved on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] Omwat and developed their own civilization, erroneously believing themselves to be the only intelligent species in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. During the early stages of the species' cultural development, Omwat unified under a single, planet-wide government. This [[Politics/Legends|political]] arrangement allowed the species to avoid the civil wars that plagued species native to other worlds.<ref name="AAUAA" />

At some point in the remote past, [[Starship/Legends|starships]] from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] visited Omwat and abducted a number of Omwati. These individuals were eventually transplanted to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], where they lived in a ghetto. Later, the Republic lost all information about Omwat, and the planet's denizens likewise forgot about the Republic.<ref name="AAUAA" />

On their homeworld, the Omwati began building honeycomb-like cities through the planet's surface and devoted their time to advancing the sciences, arts, and technologies. Eventually, the Omwati became a technological society; although they still lagged far behind the standards of the galaxy at large, they avoided overwhelming the natural resources of Omwat.<ref name="AAUAA" />

===Tarkin and the Omwati===
During the last years of the Galactic Republic, Omwat was rediscovered and visited by a promising Republic [[Republic officer/Legends|military officer]] by the name of [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]]. The Omwati, after some initial surprise, welcomed the [[Alien/Legends|alien]] visitor. Tarkin soon understood that the blue-skinned natives were related to the Omwati living on other planets, but he kept that information from them; as Tarkin was familiar with the mental brilliance and successes of Omwati children, he thought he could profit from the discovery<ref name="AAUAA" /> by controlling some promising, creative young minds and using them for his own benefit.<ref name="T1" />

Tarkin kept the planet a secret except from all but a few close collaborators. To gain the Omwati's trust, Tarkin gave them information about history, culture, and technology in the Republic for them to study, and he promised to return with more ships. Any reference to Omwati on other planets was carefully censored by Tarkin's agents.<ref name="AAUAA" />

Later, the Republic was [[Declaration of a New Order|replaced]] by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] rewarded Tarkin with the [[Grand Moff/Legends|dominion]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], an area that included Omwat. Tarkin decided it was time to make use of the Omwati, and, ten years after his first contact, he returned to Omwat. Tarkin ordered a training center built in Omwat's [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]]. Then, he threatened the Omwati with a [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|bombardment]] of the planetary surface, thus destroying all the planet's cities, unless the Omwati performed intelligence tests on their children and surrendered their several hundred brightest youth to Tarkin. The Omwati agreed, but at the same time they secretly began a [[Realspace/Legends|space]] program to reach Tarkin's [[Satellite/Legends|satellite]] through their own means. Omwat's [[Gravity/Legends|gravitational]] pull, however, proved a significant problem to these Omwati engineers.<ref name="AAUAA" />

Ten of these Omwati children, coming from different cities, were trained for two years in the orbiting sphere by some of the best [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] and engineers Tarkin could assemble,<ref name="T1" /> including [[Nasdra Magrody]]<ref name="CJ1">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']], Chapter 1</ref> and [[Ohran Keldor]].<ref name="CJ12">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']], Chapter 12</ref> The youths knew that their knowledge would be thoroughly tested and, should any of them fail a test, his or her native city would be destroyed and the failed student [[Death/Legends|executed]]. Such was the fate of nine of the children, including [[Pillik]]. Only the young Qwi Xux passed all the tests presented to her. As a reward, Tarkin sent Xux to his secret research center, the [[Maw Installation]], where she would work with famed engineer [[Bevel Lemelisk]] developing weaponry for the Empire.<ref name="T1" /> The galactic government covered up Xux's involvement by listing all of the abducted Omwati children, including Xux, as deceased.<ref name="AAUAA" />

===Omwat after Tarkin===
Tarkin and many of his closer collaborators were killed during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. As the orbital training center at Omwat was mostly a secret, it was abandoned. The Omwati managed to reach it at some point between [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]] and [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. The Empire had recorded the death of all but ten of Tarkin's abducted children. However, the Omwati refused to believe the reports and decided to search for the missing younglings. They also adopted whatever technology they could from Tarkin's [[Space station/Legends|space station]], which allowed them to research ships that could reach distant [[Star/Legends|stars]].<ref name="AAUAA" />

In [[14 ABY/Legends|14 ABY]], the Omwati built their first [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] and entered the galaxy at large. They first spread terror in nearby settlements and ports, as their reasons and motivations for expansion were not understood. Finally, Omwati [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] were contacted by [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomats]], who were eager to listen to their story. The New Republic used this chance to document the atrocities performed by the Empire on yet another planet. The Omwati were then welcomed by their "cousins" on Coruscant and other planets.<ref name="AAUAA" />

Soon afterward, using the information provided by Tarkin about [[The Force/Legends|the Force]], the Omwati began to develop their own tradition of using the mystical energy field. This collective was formed and had several members as of [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]].<ref name="AAUAA" />

==Omwati in the galaxy==
[[File:FinnCouple.png|thumb|right|200px|The Finns were Coruscant-dwelling Omwati.]]
{{Quote|What's a nice girl like you doing in a place like this?|Han Solo, to Qwi Xux|<ref name="T1" />}}
As a number of Omwati left their planet in some remote time of the Old Republic,<ref name="AAUAA" /> Omwati were a common sight on several planets of the galaxy during the time before the Empire. There were Omwati on Coruscant in [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]], as exemplified in traffic coordinator [[Kodo Finn]] and his wife, [[Aleema Finn]].<ref name="EAP">''[[Evasive Action: Prey]]''</ref> The Omwati Jedi Tannis operated on the planet of [[Teya IV]] around [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]].<ref name="AJ">{{JournalCite|11|The Most Dangerous Foe}}</ref>

After 14 ABY, many Omwati traveled through the galaxy, looking for the missing children who had been kidnapped by Tarkin. Most of these Omwati were peaceful.<ref name="AAUAA" />

Omwati had the potential to be [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]], and some Omwati followed Force traditions that sometimes led them off their homeworld. During the days of the Old Republic, several members of the species joined the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], including [[Tannis (Jedi)|Tannis]]<ref name="AJ" /> and [[Bleth Fahr]].<ref name="CD">{{LivingForce|Coruscani Dawn}}</ref> During the reign of the Empire, an [[Unidentified Omwati shaman|Omwati]] [[Shaman/Legends|shaman]] was on the planet [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]].<ref name="SWG">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=terminal||Girl Abducted by Omwat Shaman}}</ref> Under the New Republic's rule, the Omwati developed [[Omwati Force tradition|their own Force tradition]], taught on the planet Omwat.<ref name="AAUAA" /> This did not stop some Omwati, such as [[Tiu Zax]], from joining [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker's]] subsequent [[New Jedi Order|Jedi Order]] to become [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]].<ref name="L1" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Mermeia.jpg|thumb|right|The inspiration for the Omwati]]
{{Quote|And, in an unusual spinoff, I was thinking of the Diana Ross glittery-feathery alien when I designed my lovely female alien scientist Qwi Xux.|Kevin J. Anderson|<ref name="I Have a Bad Feeling About This!">{{InsiderCite|106|I Have a Bad Feeling About This!}}</ref>}}
The Omwati first appeared in the [[1994]] novel ''[[Jedi Search]]'', written by [[Kevin J. Anderson]], primarily represented by the scientist character Qwi Xux.<ref name="T1" /> Anderson's original visual model for the appearance of Qwi Xux was [[Mermeia]], as portrayed by [[Diahann Carroll]] in ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''. When referring to this in an interview, Anderson likened Mermeia with celebrity singer [[Wikipedia:Diana Ross|Diana Ross]].<ref name="mermeia">{{WebCite|url=http://www.lucasfan.com/swtv/index3.html|text=Star Wars Holiday Special Opinions|work=[https://web.archive.org/web/19981212015351/http://lucasfan.com LucasFan.com]|archivedate=20200120144211|nolive=1}}</ref><ref name="I Have a Bad Feeling About This!" /> The first graphical depiction of an Omwati was drawn by [[Michael Butkus]] for ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''.

The ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] guides ''[[Alien Anthology]]'' and ''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]'' allow players to take on the role of Omwati characters. The sourcebooks both describe the Omwati in similar terms, including game statistics: Omwati characters receive a bonus to their intellectual knowledge and perception but suffer a slight penalty to their physical strength. Although ''Alien Anthology'' does not give them any further benefits, ''Ultimate Alien Anthology'' provides the Omwati with an additional benefit to their skills to fix machines and use computers.
